summary: Streaming tool-call arguments appear truncated mid-stream (JSON parse fails unless waiting for final tool_call)
body:
Issue summary
AcmeAI reports that, when using streaming + tool calling, tool-call arguments sometimes appear truncated mid-stream. Their app attempts to parse tool arguments as JSON as soon as a tool call is first observed; during streaming the arguments field is delivered as partial deltas, causing intermittent JSON parse errors (e.g., unexpected end of input) and resulting in failed tool execution.

Impact
- Tool calls fail intermittently (estimated 5–15% depending on prompt length and tool args size), causing user-visible errors in their agent workflow.
- Increased retries and latency; customer is evaluating Redwood and flagged this as a launch blocker.

Environment
- Deployment: Dedicated capacity
- Region: us-east-1
- Endpoint: /v1/responses (stream=true)
- SDK: Python (customer code is based on our older streaming snippet)
- Models observed: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct, rw-qwen2.5-72b-instruct

Customer report
Customer expects tool_call.arguments to be complete JSON for each streaming event. Instead, the arguments arrive incrementally and are not valid JSON until the final tool-call event has been received.

Steps to reproduce (support repro)
1) Create a tool with a moderately sized JSON argument payload (nested object, 1–2 KB serialized).
2) Call the model with stream=true and tools=[...].
3) In the stream handler, parse tool_call.arguments as JSON each time a tool-call delta arrives (instead of buffering).
4) Observe JSONDecodeError / parse failures.

Observed behavior
- Streaming delivers tool-call argument deltas. Example from customer logs (redacted):

Event: response.output_item.added
output_item: {"type":"tool_call","id":"call_01H...","name":"lookup_customer","arguments":"{\"customer_id\":\"acme_"}

Event: response.output_item.delta
delta: {"tool_call_id":"call_01H...","arguments_delta":"ai_439\",\"include\":{\"billing\":true"}

Event: response.output_item.delta
delta: {"tool_call_id":"call_01H...","arguments_delta":",\"usage\":true}}"}

If the app parses after the first event or between deltas, it fails with truncated JSON.

Expected behavior
- Streaming semantics: tool-call arguments may be partial until the tool call is completed; apps should buffer deltas and parse only after tool-call completion (or the final response event).
- Examples/docs should make this explicit and provide a safe assembly pattern.

Additional notes
- Customer was following a snippet that treated tool-call arguments as a complete JSON field per event (legacy / inconsistent across languages).
- Similar symptoms were mentioned in SUP-18436 (structured output parse errors), but this ticket is specifically about tool-call arguments during streaming.

Workaround (provided to customer)
- Buffer tool-call argument deltas per tool_call_id; only JSON-parse once a terminal event indicates completion (e.g., response.output_item.done / tool_call done) or after receiving response.completed.
- Add guardrails: on JSON parse failure, keep buffering (do not execute tool) unless a terminal event has been received.
- Log and surface tool_call_id + partial length for debugging; consider retry if stream disconnects before completion.

Request
- Confirm canonical streaming semantics and provide updated example code.
- Validate whether SDK helper(s) or docs need correction to prevent customers parsing too early.

Attachments / logs
- Customer-provided log excerpt included above (IDs redacted). Full raw transcript attached in Zendesk export (internal link in comments).
comments:
2025-02-12 09:18 (Priya Shah - Support)
Acknowledged receipt. Asking AcmeAI for (1) SDK version, (2) exact code snippet for their stream handler, (3) whether they see a terminal tool-call event before parsing. Added note that streaming can deliver partial deltas and we likely need to buffer.

Internal: looping in #support and #devex; referencing ongoing examples refresh workstream.

2025-02-12 10:02 (AcmeAI - Customer)
We’re using Python (pinned to 0.9.x; can share exact later). We parse tool_call.arguments immediately when we see a tool call because docs implied it’s a single JSON blob. Example error:
JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 20 (char 19)
If we disable streaming, it works.

2025-02-12 10:24 (Owen Phillips - Support Escalations)
Reproduced with a local harness by parsing arguments on the first tool_call event. Confirmed the args field is incremental with streaming.

Proposed customer guidance:
- Buffer by tool_call_id
- Append arguments_delta
- Parse on output_item.done (or response.completed)

Also requesting DevEx confirm the event names we should cite publicly (we should align with the conventions doc).

2025-02-12 11:05 (Ibrahim Khan - SDK parity TL)
Confirmed expected semantics: tool call arguments are streamed as deltas; they are not guaranteed to be valid JSON until the tool call is complete. Older snippets were misleading.

Pointing to work in progress:
- Docs pitfalls section will explicitly call out partial tool args during streaming.
- SDK examples updated to include correct assembly loop.

If customer needs immediate unblock, suggest switching to non-streaming for tool-call step OR buffer deltas and parse only after terminal event.

2025-02-12 11:22 (Priya Shah - Support)
Sent workaround to AcmeAI with a minimal Python pseudo-code loop:
- tool_args[tool_call_id] += arguments_delta
- if tool_done: json.loads(tool_args[tool_call_id])
Also advised: do not treat JSON parse errors as final until you’ve received a done/completed event.

Asked customer to confirm which streaming event they receive that indicates completion in their SDK version.

2025-02-13 08:41 (AcmeAI - Customer)
Buffering works. We were missing the “done” condition; we were parsing as soon as we saw name=lookup_customer. With buffering + parse on completion, errors stopped in testing.

Request: please update docs/examples; our team copy/pasted from a guide and assumed arguments were complete per event.

2025-02-13 09:10 (Wei Chen - Hosted API Docs)
Noted. We’ll add a “Known pitfalls” callout: tool-call arguments may arrive in multiple chunks; do not parse until you have the final tool-call event. Will also add guidance for stream disconnect/retry and partial argument handling.

Tracking via docs PR redwood-docs/pr-519.

2025-02-14 14:27 (Sabrina James - SDK examples)
Python example updated to assemble tool-call args across deltas and parse only after tool_call is complete. Added a golden transcript fixture covering partial args (including a multi-chunk JSON object).
Tracking via redwood-sdk-python/pr-2874 and pr-2881.

2025-02-18 16:03 (Owen Phillips - Support Escalations)
Closing the loop with customer:
- Clarified that partial tool-call args during streaming are expected.
- Provided link to updated docs section (pending publish) and recommended upgrading SDK once the examples refresh release is out.

Also flagged that a separate edge case in final message assembly was hotfixed (redwood/pr-14680) and is relevant to structured output streams (not required for the tool-call buffering workaround).

2025-02-19 10:36 (Priya Shah - Support)
Customer confirmed they are unblocked and have updated their stream handler. Marking ticket Resolved.

Follow-ups:
- Ensure docs explicitly show the terminal condition for tool-call parsing.
- Ensure cross-language snippets use the same phrasing/event naming per streaming conventions.
resolution: Resolved with documented workaround: tool-call arguments are streamed as deltas and can be truncated mid-stream; customers must buffer arguments per tool_call_id and parse JSON only after the tool call is complete (terminal event) or on response completion. DevEx updated SDK examples and docs to prevent copy/paste parsing too early; golden tests added to lock in the expected streaming sequence.
customer_visible_next_steps: Upgrade to the next Python SDK release containing refreshed examples; follow the updated streaming + tool calling guide that buffers partial tool-call argument deltas and parses only after completion.
internal_follow_ups: Docs: publish known-pitfalls callout for partial tool args during streaming (redwood-docs/pr-519).
SDKs: keep golden transcript tests covering multi-chunk tool args (redwood-sdk-python/pr-2881).
Release comms: include this pitfall in examples refresh notes to reduce repeat tickets.
